note: Pre-written example conversation (not live AI output). Used only until the live capture arrives.
skeptic: If God is good and strong, why is there so much pain?
That does not explain a child who gets sick.
It is personal. My sister was sick for years. If God could stop it and didn't, how is that good?
People say it's all part of a plan. That sounds cold when you're the one hurting.
Then what do you actually say to someone in the middle of it?
I need to think about that. Thanks for the talk.

coach.nudge: Name what the skeptic is really asking: why this pain, not just any pain.
coach.outline:
Agree that the pain is real.
Say what you don't know.
Point to a God who entered suffering, not one who watched from a distance.
Ask what is behind the question for them.
coach.sample: I won't pretend that makes sense of a sick child. I don't know why God allows each thing. What I hold on to is that God did not stay far from pain. In Jesus he stepped into it. Can I ask if this question is personal for you?

review.covered: You named the pain as real, admitted what you do not know, and turned toward the person by asking if the question was personal.
review.couldAdd: When they mentioned their sister, slow down and ask what that time was like before offering hope.
review.possibleAnswer: Pain is real, and Christians don't claim to know every reason God allows it. We hold on to a God who entered suffering in Jesus and promises it won't have the last word.
